decision_rule: Report condition-specific evidence only. Do not convert the final results into a universal method ranking and do not retune frozen settings on Day 25 test cases.
limitations: Day 25 final synthetic test cases use known transforms and simulated modality mappings; they do not replace real multimodal validation.

MI and ECC use their own previously frozen preprocessing and optimizer configurations. The image geometry and appearance condition are shared, but method-specific preprocessing is part of each frozen method pipeline.
Rigid and affine results must be interpreted separately because the motion models solve different geometric problems.
Optimizer execution success and within-tolerance geometric correctness remain separate fields.
The frozen MI configuration uses full sampling, so Day 25 does not select or rerun a random seed for final-test accuracy. Day 22 stochastic evidence is carried forward separately.
RIRE evidence is not included in the synthetic TRE ranking because verified landmarks or masks are not integrated.
next_step: Week 5 is complete. Proceed to Week 6 unified evaluation and reproducible benchmarking without retuning the frozen Week 5 final-test configurations.
purpose: Run a frozen final synthetic multimodal benchmark for rigid and affine MI, compare against compatible historical ECC baselines on the same test cases, carry forward the Day 22 stochastic evidence, and keep real RIRE evidence separate.

real_rire_evidence.interpretation: Day 24 validates the technical 3D rigid MI path on the prepared real RIRE CT/MR-T1 pair: both initializations execute, return plausible rigid transforms, preserve the fixed CT output geometry, and satisfy metadata checks. The two initialization paths converge to very similar transforms and final MI values, which supports initialization consistency for this pair. Geometry initialization is more efficient here, but no anatomical accuracy ranking is claimed. The decrease in physical field-of-view coverage after registration is preserved as a limitation and requires caution because physical domain overlap is not anatomical ground truth.
real_rire_evidence.note: Real RIRE evidence remains descriptive and technically validated. It is not mixed into the synthetic TRE-based method comparison because verified landmarks or masks are not integrated.
observations: Both geometry and identity initialization completed successfully and passed the configured technical validation checks.
Both initializations converged to nearly the same rigid physical transform, with about 5.43 degrees rotation magnitude and 33.5 mm translation magnitude.
Geometry initialization required fewer optimizer iterations and lower runtime than identity initialization on this pair.
The minimum bidirectional physical field-of-view coverage decreased from about 0.818 before registration to about 0.668 after registration for both variants.
The reduced physical domain overlap is retained as evidence and is not interpreted as anatomical failure or success because verified reference landmarks or masks are not integrated.

title: Integrated Week 5 multimodal benchmark and closure evidence
conclusions: On the frozen final synthetic test set, Mutual Information produced more within-tolerance registrations than ECC for both rigid and affine models.
Rigid Mutual Information reached 5 of 6 within tolerance versus 4 of 6 for rigid ECC; affine Mutual Information reached 6 of 7 versus 3 of 7 for affine ECC.
Intensity inversion exposed a clear condition-specific difference: Mutual Information passed the rigid and affine inversion cases while ECC failed to return a valid estimate.
The affine bias-field case was recovered by Mutual Information but not ECC, and the affine partial-overlap inversion case was also recovered only by Mutual Information.
Edge-emphasized appearance remained a shared failure mode: both methods were outside tolerance for rigid and affine edge-emphasized cases.
Mutual Information was generally slower than ECC, so the final evidence supports condition-specific method selection rather than a universal ranking.
The real RIRE CT/MR-T1 result remains technical physical-space evidence only because verified landmarks or masks are not integrated.
